To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) soil physicochemical characteristics influence microbial community distribution; (2) soil sampling strategies are crucial for obtaining representative soil samples; (3) the soil matrix interacts with DNA and affects its extraction; (4) DNA extraction methods influence the bacterial community profiles obtained and (5) metagenomic sequence analyses are still in their infancy and need to be optimized.
the microbial diversity perceived by metagenomic analyses is strongly affected by the physicochemical properties of the soil matrix.
the soil matrix is the main factor that influences the extraction of microbial DNA and, consequently, the perceived microbial distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how soil physicochemical characteristics affect microbial distribution and the subsequent extraction and analysis of the metagenome.

understanding how soil physicochemical characteristics and soil DNA extraction procedures influence microbial diversity estimates and how to optimize the extraction and analysis of soil metagenomes to obtain the best possible microbial diversity estimates.
the bias inherent to metagenome 'handling' and the strategies that can be used to reduce this bias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
metagenomics approaches are still in their infancy, with a long way to go to be fully exploited and understood.

soil metagenomics is a powerful tool to investigate the microbial diversity present in soil, provided that the limitations of the method are taken into account and appropriate precautions and methods are implemented.
soil metagenome analysis is not yet a routine technique, although some of the steps in this process have reached a high level of standardization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the microbial diversity of a given soil is a complex function of the physicochemical properties of this soil and that the metagenome processing methods used to access this diversity should take this complexity into account.
soil metagenome analysis requires careful sampling strategies to avoid sampling bias, and the use of optimized DNA extraction methods to avoid bias in the perceived microbial diversity.
soil metagenomics has the potential to provide a true picture of the microbial communities in the soil.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the soil matrix and its physicochemical properties are key factors that should be taken into consideration when studying soil microbial communities by using metagenomics approaches. © 2016, Springer Science+Business Media New York.
soil microbial diversity cannot be fully described using metagenomics approaches alone.
soil metagenome analyses are biased and that the bias depends on the physicochemical properties of the soil.
